title: Anti-Trivialization Machines of the Future
lines: Anti-Trivialization Machines of the Future asks how institutions can protect serious attention.
Its argument concerns the organization of influence, rather than individual failures of willpower.
The book explores cognitive assistance, attention rules, provenance, and institutions for longer time horizons.
It favors plural, limited institutions over one authority deciding what everyone should consider important.
Readers can examine these proposals without accepting that their eventual arrival is guaranteed.

title: An institutional problem
lines: More information does not automatically produce a greater capacity for sustained judgment.
The book examines incentives that interrupt attention, compress time, and reward immediate response.
It places AI within that institutional setting instead of treating distraction as a new personal defect.
The question is how important problems can remain visible long enough for collective action.
That shift explains why the proposed countermeasures extend beyond better individual habits.

title: Several institutions, limited powers
lines: The proposals include cognitive assistance aligned with declared goals and limits on adaptive influence.
Other institutions would support provenance, protected time, and longer decision horizons.
Different communities require different arrangements for attention and evidence.
The book rejects one central authority assigning seriousness or truth to everyone.
Its alternative depends on plural institutions that can inspect and counterbalance one another.

title: Read for protected attention
lines: Begin with the distinction between condemning entertainment and preserving the capacity for serious thought.
Follow the proposed institutions alongside the power they would themselves acquire.
The book does not establish that these arrangements will inevitably appear.
It asks what societies would need to build if sustained judgment is to remain possible.
Read it to examine attention as a shared institutional responsibility, not merely a private resource.
